derivations.name: Exact laws, re-derived from scratch
derivations.statement: S_4 cycle-type law by brute force over all 24 permutations with an own cycle tracer; A_4 by inversion-count parity; D_4 by cycle-decomposing the raw `perm` 4-tuples of every non-ramified row of BOTH archived a20e48 N1 logs.

derivations.name: ITEM 1 -- exact finer-resolution N_required, frozen floor lifted to N=1
derivations.method: Full enumeration of the multinomial support (C(N+4,4) count vectors) with exact Fraction masses; threshold = smallest v with F_null(v) >= 0.95; reject if LR > threshold. No Monte Carlo.
derivations.closed_form: N_required = ceil(ln(alpha)/ln(1-m)), m = S_4-mass of the cycle types the subgroup excludes. Verified EXACT against enumeration for all four subgroups (m = 1/2, 1/3, 7/12, 5/6).
derivations.conclusion: The contract's central ordering prediction N_required(D4) > N_required(A4) is TRUE at finer resolution (8 > 5, ratio 1.6). It was invisible only because the frozen search floor N=10 sits above BOTH answers. The A_4 curve is a step function because cycle type determines parity in S_4 and P_A4 = P_S4(.|even), so the statistic carries exactly one bit per draw.

derivations.name: ITEM 3 -- rejection-direction sanity check, exact, two conventions
derivations.conclusion: The Executor's convention (threshold = 0.95 quantile of the null LR distribution; LR > threshold => 'it's the subgroup') is Neyman-Pearson CORRECT. LR is strictly increasing in the count of the category the sub law favours. Under the handoff's contradictory prose convention power collapses to ~0 and at N>=20 falls strictly below its own size (anti-informative); applied to the real pairs it gives power 0.00000 for BOTH, which would have inverted the entire record.

derivations.name: ITEM 4 -- NULL-1 mutation test
derivations.object_identity_check: sub_law as a DISTINCT list with identical values gives the identical thr=0, FPR=0.0, power=0.0. The degeneracy is numerical EQUALITY of the two laws, not Python object identity as the report's mechanism_note states.
derivations.conclusion: NULL-1 as executed detects exactly one bug (the tie rule) and is blind to every quantile corruption. NULL-2 is byte-identical in construction, so the record has one degenerate control reported twice.

supplied_replacement_control.sub_law: S_4 with mass eps moved from 3-cycle to double-transposition; all five categories strictly positive
supplied_replacement_control.reading: Empirical size sits on the nominal alpha=0.05 at every N. This is the calibration evidence the record's own controls never produced.

derivations.name: ITEM 2 -- deliberately weakened sub laws (proves the test is not trivially separating)
derivations.conclusion: PASSES. N_required grows without bound as the sub law approaches S_4, scaling as ~1/D_KL over four orders of magnitude, with empirical size pinned at 0.046-0.050 throughout. The N=10 saturation is a genuine fact about how much S_4 mass A_4 and D_4 exclude, not a degenerate test.

derivations.name: ITEM 5 -- proves-too-much on Step 4b's N=2000 classifier

cases.object: resampled from V4 law (truth: NOT D4)
resampled from C4 law (truth: NOT D4)
S4 conditioned on no 3-cycle (not a group law)

derivations.conclusion: The classifier is NOT a rubber stamp -- 100% detection of genuine D4, 0% false alarm on genuine S4 at N=2000, so Step 4b's clean pass is real. But at N=2000 it reduces to 'did I see a 3-cycle', so it certifies 'not S_4' rather than 'is D_4'; V4, C4, a non-group law and a 2000/2000-transpositions sample are all labelled D_4, and an A_4 sample is labelled S_4.

derivations.name: OBJ-5 -- Step 4a is structurally vacuous; block-resampling control finds real structure
derivations.reading_a: Uniform with-replacement resampling is i.i.d. by construction, so it agrees with the i.i.d. synthetic at EVERY N, not merely at the degenerate N=10 the Executor disclosed. Step 4a cannot detect the correlation structure HEUR-MONO-CONV-1 names as its gap.
derivations.structural_confirmation: The 211 per-e1-row identity counts (211 points per row, p=211) have variance 6.97 against a binomial 24.95 (ratio 0.28) and range only over 23..35.
derivations.null_object_control: The identical measurement on the SAME multiset with the order destroyed by a shuffle gives ratio 1.00 +/- 0.06 at N <= 211. The effect is a property of the census ordering, not of the estimator. Claims are restricted to N <= p = 211, where enough disjoint windows remain that the shuffled null still reads 1.00.
derivations.conclusion: The archived N1 point-parametrized census is significantly UNDER-DISPERSED relative to i.i.d., so HEUR-MONO-CONV-1 is measurably false as stated for the N1-style member. The deviation is conservative for this record's use (structured sampling is more informative per draw, not less), N1 is exhaustive so no verdict depends on it, and the N3/N5-style members draw independent coefficients where i.i.d. is far more plausible. What it overturns is the claim that Step 4a validated the heuristic.

derivations.name: OBJ-2 -- Chernoff-Stein cross-reference audit

kl_directions.D_KL(P_S4||P_sub): +infinity for BOTH (each subgroup assigns zero to a class S_4 gives positive mass)

derivations.objection: Stein's lemma's type-II exponent at fixed type-I is D_KL(P_null||P_alt), which is +infinity here, so the invoked asymptotic does not apply to this record's object. The formula over-predicts N_required by 2.2x (11 vs 5) and 1.7x (14 vs 8), and BOTH values exceed the frozen floor N=10, directly contradicting the record's own measured power=1.0 at N=10 -- a conflict the report does not flag while presenting the numbers as corroboration.
derivations.where_the_formula_is_good: On fully-supported alternatives the product N_required * D_KL(Q||P) sits between 7.6 and 8.2 against ln(1/(alpha*beta)) = 7.60 across four orders of magnitude in N. That agreement is a numerical coincidence of alpha=0.05, beta=0.01 with the local-asymptotic constant (z_0.95+z_0.99)^2 * 2D/(2D)^2 = 7.89/D, not a validation of the derivation.

derivations.name: OBJ-3 -- nearby-object control across the transitive proper subgroups of S_4
derivations.conclusion: N_required is a strictly decreasing function of excluded S_4 mass and is indifferent to primitivity: two imprimitive groups need FEWER draws than the primitive A_4. The record's 'primitive vs imprimitive' framing is falsified as an explanation. Separately, D4-real and D4-Haar give the SAME N_required, so the record's confounder about the non-Haar law is immaterial to its own headline metric.

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""RED TEAM RT-20260830-909b4e -- minimal self-contained reproduction of every
load-bearing number in the report. Pure stdlib. Runs in ~2 s.
Usage: python3 repro.py /path/to/crypto-autoresearcher"""
import sys, json, math, itertools, random, statistics
from fractions import Fraction
from collections import defaultdict
REPO = sys.argv[1] if len(sys.argv) > 1 else "."
CT_OF = {(1,1,1,1):0,(2,1,1):1,(2,2):2,(3,1):3,(4,):4}
def cyc(p):
    n=len(p); s=[False]*n; L=[]
    for i in range(n):
        if s[i]: continue
        l=0; j=i
        while not s[j]: s[j]=True; j=p[j]; l+=1
        L.append(l)
    return tuple(sorted(L, reverse=True))
def par(p): return sum(1 for i in range(4) for j in range(i+1,4) if p[i]>p[j])%2
def law(el):
    c=[0]*5
    for p in el: c[CT_OF[cyc(p)]]+=1
    return [Fraction(x,len(el)) for x in c]
def pfc(cs):
    p=list(range(4))
    for c in cs:
        for i in range(len(c)): p[c[i]]=c[(i+1)%len(c)]
    return tuple(p)
ALL=list(itertools.permutations(range(4)))
S4=law(ALL); A4=law([p for p in ALL if par(p)==0])
V4=law([pfc([]),pfc([[0,1],[2,3]]),pfc([[0,2],[1,3]]),pfc([[0,3],[1,2]])])
C4=law([pfc([]),pfc([[0,1,2,3]]),pfc([[0,2],[1,3]]),pfc([[0,3,2,1]])])
cnt=[0]*5; stream=[]
with open(REPO+"/experiments/EXP-MONO-a20e48/runs/RUN-MONO-a20e48-1/per_base_point_log/N1_k1_exhaustive.jsonl") as f:
    for line in f:
        r=json.loads(line)
        if r.get("class") is None: continue
        i=CT_OF[cyc(tuple(r["perm"]))]; cnt[i]+=1; stream.append(i)
D4=[Fraction(x,sum(cnt)) for x in cnt]
NEG=float("-inf")
def lrt(P,Q): return [0.0 if (q==0 and p==0) else (NEG if q==0 else math.log(float(q)/float(p))) for p,q in zip(P,Q)]
def lrv(c,t): return NEG if any(c[i]>0 and t[i]==NEG for i in range(5)) else round(sum(c[i]*t[i] for i in range(5) if c[i]),12)
def comps(n,k):
    if k==1: yield (n,); return
    for i in range(n+1):
        for r in comps(n-i,k-1): yield (i,)+r
def exact(P,Q,N,alpha=Fraction(1,20)):
    t=lrt(P,Q); mn=defaultdict(Fraction); ms=defaultdict(Fraction)
    for c in comps(N,5):
        oP=all(c[i]==0 for i in range(5) if P[i]==0); oQ=all(c[i]==0 for i in range(5) if Q[i]==0)
        if not(oP or oQ): continue
        v=lrv(c,t); co=math.factorial(N)
        for x in c: co//=math.factorial(x)
        if oP:
            m=Fraction(co)
            for i in range(5):
                if c[i]: m*=P[i]**c[i]
            mn[v]+=m
        if oQ:
            m=Fraction(co)
            for i in range(5):
                if c[i]: m*=Q[i]**c[i]
            ms[v]+=m
    vs=sorted(mn); cu=Fraction(0); thr=vs[-1]
    for v in vs:
        cu+=mn[v]
        if cu>=1-alpha: thr=v; break
    return thr, float(sum(m for v,m in mn.items() if v>thr)), float(sum(m for v,m in ms.items() if v>thr))
print("S4 =",[str(x) for x in S4]); print("A4 =",[str(x) for x in A4])
print("D4 counts =",cnt,"n =",sum(cnt)); print("D4 =",[float(x) for x in D4])
print("\nEXACT power/size, floor lifted to N=1:")
for nm,Q in (("S4_vs_A4",A4),("S4_vs_D4",D4),("S4_vs_C4",C4),("S4_vs_V4",V4)):
    row=[]; nreq=None
    for N in range(1,16):
        th,sz,pw=exact(S4,Q,N); row.append(round(pw,4))
        if nreq is None and pw>=0.99: nreq=N
    m=float(sum(S4[i] for i in range(5) if Q[i]==0))
    print("  %-9s m=%.4f N_required=%s closed_form=%d power(N=1..15)=%s"%(
        nm,m,nreq,math.ceil(math.log(0.05)/math.log(1-m)),row))
print("\nExact size at N=10 (compare Executor's Monte Carlo):")
for nm,Q,mc in (("S4_vs_A4",A4,(0.0007,0.00085)),("S4_vs_D4",D4,(0.01675,0.01635))):
    m=float(sum(S4[i] for i in range(5) if Q[i]==0)); ex=(1-m)**10
    se=math.sqrt(ex*(1-ex)/20000)
    print("  %s exact=%.8f  MC=%.5f(%+.2f SE) %.5f(%+.2f SE)"%(nm,ex,mc[0],(mc[0]-ex)/se,mc[1],(mc[1]-ex)/se))
print("\nChernoff-Stein audit (Executor's formula vs the correct closed form):")
for nm,Q in (("A4",A4),("D4",D4)):
    d=sum(float(q)*math.log(float(q)/float(p)) for q,p in zip(Q,S4) if q>0)
    m=float(sum(S4[i] for i in range(5) if Q[i]==0))
    print("  %s D_KL(Q||S4)=%.6f  ln(1/(ab))/D_KL=%.4f->%d   ln(a)/ln(1-m)=%.4f->%d"%(
        nm,d,math.log(1/(0.05*0.01))/d,
        math.ceil(math.log(1/(0.05*0.01))/d),
        math.log(0.05)/math.log(1-m),math.ceil(math.log(0.05)/math.log(1-m))))
print("\nBlock-vs-iid dispersion of the identity count, disjoint windows, with shuffled null:")
M=len(stream); p=cnt[0]/M; sh=stream[:]; random.Random(4242).shuffle(sh)
for N in (10,50,100,211):
    k=M//N
    v=lambda s: statistics.variance([sum(1 for j in range(N) if s[i*N+j]==0) for i in range(k)])
    th=N*p*(1-p)*(1-(N-1)/(M-1))
    print("  N=%-4d windows=%-5d theory=%.3f real=%.3f (%.3f) shuffled=%.3f (%.3f)"%(
        N,k,th,v(stream),v(stream)/th,v(sh),v(sh)/th))
